title: Gabber exactness of the local oriented-product projection
statement:
Let $a:A\to S$ be a local morphism of strictly henselian local schemes (it sends the closed point $x$ of $A$ to the closed point $s$ of $S$), and let $b:B\to S$ be any morphism of schemes. Use their small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and put $P=A_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal], with second projection $p_2$. Let $\epsilon:B_{\mathrm{Et}}\to\mathbf{Set}$ be the canonical geometric morphism. For each sheaf of sets $F$ on $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$, pullback by $b$ of the natural map from the constant sheaf with value $F_s=\Gamma(S_{\mathrm{Et}},F)$ to $F$ defines a $2$-morphism $b\Rightarrow s\epsilon$ (the convention on $2$-morphisms is that of the universal-product node). Together with $x\epsilon:B_{\mathrm{Et}}\to A_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $1_{B_{\mathrm{Et}}}$ it defines a section $\sigma:B_{\mathrm{Et}}\to P$ of $p_2$. For every commutative ring $\Lambda$ and every sheaf $H$ of constant-$\Lambda$ modules on $P$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the canonical map
$$p_{2,*}H\longrightarrow\sigma^*H$$
obtained by applying $p_{2,*}$ to the adjunction unit $H\to\sigma_*\sigma^*H$ is an isomorphism, naturally in $H$. In particular $p_{2,*}$ is exact. Here strictly henselian means henselian with separably closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and geometric closed points are as in [def-weil-geometric-point].

source.place: Exposé XI 2.2, construction (2.b)--(2.f), Proposition 2.3 and Corollary 2.3.1, printed pp. 177--178; small etale topoi have enough geometric points. Also Illusie, Around the Thom--Sebastiani theorem, Proposition 1.12 (1.12.1), printed p. 13.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-strictly-henselian-open-sections-stalk] with the whole scheme as the open, separately to $A$ and $S$. Thus $\Gamma(A,G)\to G_x$ and $\Gamma(S,F)\to F_s$ are natural bijections for all set sheaves. Choose compatible geometric closed points, so $ax=s$; the local hypothesis is precisely what permits this. Write $\epsilon_S:S_{\mathrm{Et}}\to\mathbf{Set}$ for the canonical morphism. The counit $\epsilon_S^{-1}\Gamma(S,F)\to F$, after the second bijection, is a natural map $(s\epsilon_S)^{-1}F\to F$. It is the inverse-image mate of $c_s:1\Rightarrow s\epsilon_S$ by [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Its restriction at $s$ is the identity: a constant global-section germ is that same section under $\Gamma(S,F)\cong F_s$.

source.place: XI 2.1 and 2.2, (2.a)--(2.b); locality of scheme topoi: Stacks 03QO, lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian

proof.text: Pull this mate back by $b$ to get $b\Rightarrow s\epsilon$, since $\epsilon_Sb=\epsilon$. Apply [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] to $x\epsilon$, $1_{B_{\mathrm{Et}}}$ and this $2$-morphism. It gives $\sigma:B_{\mathrm{Et}}\to P$ and $p_2\sigma\cong1$. For constant coefficients use [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]: the ring identifications and module units agree with these inverse-image units and commute with composition. Therefore $p_{2,*}\sigma_*\cong1$ on constant-$\Lambda$ modules, and applying $p_{2,*}$ to $H\to\sigma_*\sigma^*H$ gives the stated natural $\Lambda$-linear map $\gamma_H:p_{2,*}H\to\sigma^*H$.

Use the small triple site of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] and put $k(W)=(A\to S\leftarrow W)$ for $W\in B_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Its projection formula is $p_2^{-1}(h_W)=h_{k(W)}^\#$, where the triple representable is sheafified. Indeed $h_W$ is a sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf]. The adjunction, the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] give
$$(p_{2,*}H)(W)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_W,p_{2,*}H)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_{k(W)}^\#,H)=H(k(W))$$
on underlying sets. This identification respects the module operations, which are defined on sections, so it is an identification of $\Lambda$-modules, natural in $W,H$.

source.place: XI 1.3 and the two colimit formulas in the proof of Proposition 2.3

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $y$ of $B$ and put $t=\sigma y$. For a triple $Z=(U\to V\leftarrow W)$, the inverse-image formula of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal], applied to $\sigma$, shows that a lift of $t$ to $h_Z^\#$ consists of $u\in U_x$ and $w\in W_y$ whose images in $(b^{-1}h_V)_y$ agree; the image of $u$ uses the mate of $c_s$. Here representable stalks are geometric lifts by [lem-galois-stalk-representable]. By step 1, $u$ extends uniquely to $\widetilde u:A\to U$. Its image in $V_s$ extends uniquely to $\widetilde v:S\to V$. These are actual scheme sections by [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf]. Their images in $\Gamma(A,a^{-1}h_V)$ agree, since their germs at $x$ agree and step 1 is injective. With [lem-galois-inverse-image-representable] this says that $\widetilde u$ and $a^*\widetilde v$ have exactly the compatibility required for the first two components of a triple morphism.

source.place: XI Proposition 2.3, proof: explicit refinement underlying the asserted cofinality of neighbourhoods

proof.text:
The section $\widetilde v$ gives a section $v_B:B\to B\times_SV$. Form
$$W_0=W\times_{B\times_SV}B,$$
using the structural map from $W$ and $v_B$. All three objects and maps are in $B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ by [lem-galois-inverse-image-representable]; finite limits in this site are scheme fibre products by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], so $W_0\to B$ is an etale object. The equality at $y$ in step 4 gives a lift $w_0$ of $y$ to $W_0$, by the fibre universal property. The maps $\widetilde u$, $\widetilde v$, $W_0\to W$ now define a morphism $k(W_0)\to Z$ taking the lift $w_0$ to the chosen lift of $t$. Thus every pointed triple neighbourhood has a pointed refinement of the form $k(W_0)$. This constructs the refinement rather than assuming a cofinality assertion.

source.place: XI Proposition 2.3, proof: the neighbourhoods with first two entries final are cofinal

proof.text: By [lem-trf-site-point-fibre], $H_t$ is the filtered colimit of $H(Z)$ over pointed triple neighbourhoods, while $(p_{2,*}H)_y$ is the filtered colimit of $H(k(W))$ over pointed etale neighbourhoods of $y$, using step 3. The functor $k$ gives a restriction map between these colimits. It is onto: every element has a representative by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], and step 5 refines that representative to some $k(W_0)$. It is one-to-one: if representatives on $k(W_1)$ and $k(W_2)$ agree in $H_t$, that same elementwise lemma supplies a common pointed triple refinement $Z$ on which they agree. Refine $Z$ once more to $k(W_0)$ by step 5. A morphism $k(W_0)\to k(W_i)$ is precisely a morphism $W_0\to W_i$, since its $A$ and $S$ components are maps between final objects. The two representatives therefore already agree in the $y$-stalk colimit. This proves that the restriction map is bijective, hence a $\Lambda$-module isomorphism.

source.place: XI Proposition 2.3, the two identical colimits and the natural restriction map; Stacks 00YA, 00D6--00D7

proof.text: Identify this restriction map with $\gamma_{H,y}$. A section $h\in H(k(W))$ is a map $h_{k(W)}^\#\to H$. Applying $\sigma^*$ gives a section on $W$, because $\sigma^*h_{k(W)}^\#=h_W$ by $p_2\sigma=1$ and the inverse-image formula of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Evaluating that section at the chosen lift of $y$ is exactly the image in the triple stalk described by [lem-trf-site-point-fibre]. On the other hand, the adjunction unit $H\to\sigma_*\sigma^*H$ sends a map $h_{k(W)}^\#\to H$ to its pulled-back map under the adjunction, by the unit identity of [def-trf-geometric-morphism]; the same statement holds on modules by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Thus this image is precisely the germ of $\gamma_H$ on the original section. Consequently step 6 proves that the specified canonical map, rather than just some abstract comparison, is invertible on every geometric stalk of $B$.

source.place: XI 2.2 (2.f) and Proposition 2.3, final sentence identifying gamma with natural restriction

proof.text: The conservative family of geometric stalks on $B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ in [lemma-openclosed-point-ulift] now implies that $\gamma_H$ is an isomorphism. This uses enough points on the target $B_{\mathrm{Et}}$, with no quasi-compactness or coherence assumption on $B$. It is natural in $H$ because both the unit and all the restriction maps are natural. Finally [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] says that $\sigma^*$ on constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves is exact. Transporting a short exact sequence along the natural isomorphism $p_{2,*}\cong\sigma^*$ therefore proves exactness of $p_{2,*}$.

source.place: XI Corollary 2.3.1, applied using the conservative geometric points of the second factor; Stacks 03PU, theorem-exactness-stalks, and 040S, remarks-enough-points

split_report.summary: Proved Gabber’s comparison using the canonical closed-point counit, explicit final-component triple refinements, the two stalk colimits, and identification of their map with the specified adjunction unit. No new nodes: all supporting facts already exist. Statement unchanged; corrected the enough-points variable in the source corollary inside the proof.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the strict-local exact-projection input to the normal-cone specialization / external-product comparison in the proof paragraph “(1) and (2)” of lem-trf-local-term-locality, through the existing ancestry.

tool_uses.why: General representable base-change formula expresses the compatibility condition as a fibre product of etale B-schemes.
General representable-stalk evaluation identifies lifts to etale objects with stalk elements in the neighbourhood calculation.
General Yoneda identifies projection sections from the inverse-image formula; this is a categorical tool.
The general constant-coefficient lift of any geometric morphism supplies the exact module pullback and compatibility of its units; it does not replace the oriented-product argument.
The general set-sheaf local-section theorem supplies locality of A and S, with the whole scheme as the open; this unit has no replacement for that scheme-theoretic input.
General subcanonicity converts global sections of representable etale sheaves into actual sections used in the triple refinements.
The general conservative geometric-point family detects the comparison isomorphism on B, at the coefficient universe.
